name: Pont Fortificat and Placa Llibertat
tagline: The historic heart, anchored by the fortified medieval bridge
description: Besalu's postcard center, where the fortified Romanesque bridge meets the arcaded Placa Llibertat. Cobblestone lanes, golden-stone facades, and the weekly market converge here. It is the most walkable, atmospheric, and photographed part of town, but also the busiest with day-trippers between late morning and early evening.
vibe: historic and picturesque, lively by day
bestFor: short stays, sightseeing, soaking up medieval atmosphere
pros: everything within a five minute walk
cafes and restaurants right on the plaza
cons: little privacy or quiet during peak hours

name: The Call Jueu (old Jewish quarter)
tagline: Quiet lanes around the rare surviving mikveh
description: A short walk uphill from the main plaza, the old Jewish quarter holds the mikveh, one of the best-preserved ritual baths in Europe, alongside narrow residential streets that see far fewer visitors. It is a good pick for a quieter stay that still puts you inside the historic walls, close to everything but a step removed from the busiest crowds.
bestFor: travelers wanting history without the crowds, longer quiet stays
pros: much quieter than the main plaza
still a short walk to shops and restaurants
cons: very few dining options right on the doorstep

name: Riverside along the Fluvia
tagline: Green banks and swimming spots beneath the old bridge
description: The stretch of riverbank along the Fluvia, just below the fortified bridge, offers walking paths, shaded picnic spots, and informal swimming areas in summer. It feels more like countryside than town center, with a slower pace and views back up toward the stone skyline. A handful of guesthouses and rural apartments sit along this edge.
bestFor: nature lovers, families, those wanting space and quiet
pros: direct river access and swimming in summer
good views of the medieval bridge

name: Olot (nearby volcanic gateway town)
tagline: A bigger base 25 minutes away, with real infrastructure and volcano access
description: Olot is the main town of the Garrotxa comarca, about 25 to 30 minutes from Besalu by car. It has supermarkets, pharmacies, a hospital, more dining variety, and direct access to the Garrotxa Volcanic Zone Natural Park's cone-shaped hills and beech forests. Many people base themselves in Olot for practicality and day-trip into Besalu rather than the reverse.
bestFor: longer stays needing real amenities, hikers, families
pros: full range of shops and services
more affordable long-term rentals than Besalu
cons: still a drive from Girona and the coast
